# the contributor audit: complete canonical blocks and threshold variance

The statements audited here are auxiliary fixed-cap variation results,
not a proof of OC.

## Complete canonical blocks

I read `candidate b90b49210bc91c87`
in full and ran its verifier in `work/math-venv`: all 114 exact checks pass.
The zero-sum column lifts have the asserted positive canonical Hessian,
and complete groups, including their permutations and volume factors,
give one vanishing derivative sum per group. This establishes rank at
most `dh`; partial groups do not suffice, as the actual two-fiber
rank-three example shows.

The stress calculation retains every full trace: `w_z=1-F_z>=0`.
Translation and dilation stationarity supply the precise canonical
coefficients. A zero weight does not remove that fiber's measure.
The second-order alternative has the necessary multiplier quantifier:
failure of a strict acceleration gives *some* normal stress. Simultaneous
centroid contraction excludes an abnormal stress since every affected
proper or full cap has negative derivative. The generic kernel vector
then forces one stress to have positive proper support on at most `h`
selected fibers. A conclusion from one arbitrarily chosen stress with
large support would be invalid and is not made.

The actual path follows from an explicitly assumed open neighborhood
of admissible physical vertices. Thus the result does not silently
relax active convex-compatibility constraints. Strict full/empty trace
types and inactive budget slack persist by continuity. PASS within
these stated hypotheses.

## Multiple proper thresholds

I read `candidate e25e172f74df55a2`
in full and ran its verifier: all 94 exact checks pass, including both
planar Hessians and the equal global budget example.

The physical logarithmic derivative contains `d(X-1)b_i`; its square
contributes `d^2 Var(X)b_i^2`, whereas the second logarithmic derivative
contributes `-d Var(X)b_i^2`. Subtracting the nonnegative weighted cap
sum therefore gives exactly `-d(d-1)e Var(X)b_i^2`. This justifies the
sign and factor without an inference from a numerical Hessian.

The concurrent examples have positive multipliers, proper thresholds,
and threshold sum one in every group. The all-dimensional coefficient
is strictly negative for every `d>=2`. The equal-budget two-fiber
example has cap mass `17V/20` in each of six actual ambient halfspaces.
Its negative Hessian polynomial and positive principal minors agree
with direct exact expansion. The convex hull of the two freely varied
triangles has exactly its two endpoint integer fibers.

This example's actual maximum absolute depth is `4V/9`, not `17V/20`.
Each endpoint can be isolated by a finite base tilt, and its own
centroid achieves the ordinary simplex constant. Thus equal global
budgets do not restore the canonical index; criticality is an
additional hypothesis. No implication that criticality alone suffices
has been established. PASS within the stated scope.

## Identical-body paired cost

I read `candidate cf676492f27e8f72`
in full. The independent degeneracy audit also passes. The square
pyramid has exact ordinary depth `6859V/15625` at height `19/25`, and
the displayed paired cap costs `13428V/15625`, leaving gap `58V/3125`.
The centered-uniform mixture formula, both scalar regimes, horizontal
normals and complementary caps treat all directions. Full-dimensional
cap boundaries are null; the proper-cut variant keeps a strict gap.

The remaining simplex lower-diagonal identity uses a common inner
simplex and the already proved paired-centroid inequality. It applies
only on the displayed diagonal segment. It neither implies the false
general identity nor discards the common ambient tilt in a full-chain
depth calculation. PASS.

## Moving thresholds and meeting points: PASS

I read `candidate 4be2b6ba9a961a1d`
in full and ran its standard-library verifier. All 56 exact joint
critical-Hessian checks, global moment equations, six critical cap
derivatives, the explicit right inverse and rational-time witness pass.

The derivative coefficient is `d V_z (1-t)^(d-1)/r_z`; the division
by the physical radius is retained in both the constant and base
moments. Stationarity equates multiplier-weighted moment vectors,
not individual-fiber derivatives. Supporting traces are excluded
from the open smooth chamber explicitly.

For the one-fiber concurrent families, the positive weights make the
meeting points average to the simplex centroid. Their affine span
forces every joint cap-critical direction to have `v=0,T=0`, yielding
the exact negative form `-V||E||^2/m`. The translation gauge and the
normalized-secant Taylor argument justify an actual local quadratic
volume loss, including feasible sequences with first-order cap decreases.
Continuous normal directions remain fixed; this is not a result about
independent cap rotations.

For the two-fiber family the displayed endpoint threshold motions
preserve each group's affine sum and hence its covering set. The first
derivatives vanish only after the two contributions to EACH global cap
are added. The explicit right inverse uses two dilation sums followed
by zero-sum threshold adjustments; it supplies the claimed acceleration
without an assumed surjectivity. The exact positive volume gain and
strict slack of all six caps at `t=1/1000` verify an actual physical
counterexample to local maximality in this larger parameter space.
Its budgets remain noncritical, as stated.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
